diagnosis.cause: The exact-H Human creator holds the canonical per-conversation mutation lock, reuses an existing cached owner or calls SandAgentDb::open_human_conversation_store. That function probes first, then opens with recover_on_corruption=false/reject_if_corrupt=true. The old probe returns Ok immediately for any nonempty -wal or -journal and thus bypasses immutable inspection. open_configured_db -> init_configured_db then calls Connection::open, PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and schema initialization. The controlled NOTADB case retained its main-file and unrelated bytes but lost all three original sidecar files before refusal. Disabling quarantine recovery alone does not prevent writable SQLite side effects.

production_chain.role: canonical pair lock -> cached owner or open_human_conversation_store -> atomic metadata initialization -> identity validation -> cached Arc publication
probe before normal opener; recovery=false; reject_if_corrupt=true

current_existing_fix.implementation: Reject nonzero main-file lengths below 100 before opening a file handle. Track nonempty sidecars instead of returning early. Open the main file using SQLite URI mode=ro and immutable=1; when sidecars exist inspect schema_version only for SQLITE_NOTADB and leave valid/stale WAL authority to the existing WAL-aware opener. No raw byte-preservation assertion was weakened. Latest test loops cover 10 corruption/header variants within the same named test; the suite remains 12 tests.

Conversation-ID hashing moved into human_direct_conversation_id; no replacement opener or data-deletion path was introduced in the inspected create function.

current_existing_fix.minimum_action: Preserve the already-published current owner fix and its byte-preservation/valid-WAL tests. No duplicate patch needed. Await and inspect its exact-H gates before accepting.
